content.json:
# Log Analytics V1 (Classic) Table -> Data Collection Rule Wizard
This workbook helps you find Log Analytics **custom tables (classic / V1, HTTP Data Collector API)** in a workspace, review their ingestion volume, and generate + deploy a **Data Collection Rule (DCR)** so you can migrate that table's ingestion to the **Logs Ingestion API** without changing the table's existing column names.

It does this by:
1. Reading the table's *current* columns (which typically have legacy type-suffixes like `Computer_s`, `EventTime_t`).
2. Building a DCR **input stream** using *clean* column names when they are unambiguous (suffix removed, e.g. `Computer`, `EventTime`).
3. Adding a **transformation** (`project-rename`) that renames the clean input columns back to the original suffixed names, so the **output stream** matches the table's existing schema exactly - **no destination table changes required**. If suffix removal creates duplicate names, the wizard automatically uses the original unique column names in compatibility mode.

> Reference: [Custom logs migration guide](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/custom-logs-migrate) | [Data collection rule structure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-collection-rule-structure) | [Data collection transformations](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/essentials/data-collection-transformations)

**Legacy column suffix map** used to compute the clean input-stream column names and their DCR data types:

| Suffix | Legacy meaning | DCR / KQL type |
|---|---|---|
| `_s` | string | `string` |
| `_d` | number (double) | `real` |
| `_b` | boolean | `boolean` |
| `_g` | guid | `string` (Logs ingestion API stores/queries GUIDs as string) |
| `_t` | datetime | `datetime` |

Columns without a recognized suffix (e.g. `TimeGenerated`) are passed through unchanged. Reserved system columns (`_ResourceId`, `TenantId`, `Type`, `RawData`, etc.) are excluded automatically.

### Workflow
**1. Select a table**  ->  **2. Validate its schema**  ->  **3. Configure the DCR**  ->  **4. Review and deploy**

This is a single, always-loaded workspace. Later sections unlock automatically as you complete each stage, so your selections remain available while you review or change earlier choices.

# 1 | Select a V1 table
Choose a workspace, compare its classic tables, then select the table you want to migrate.

## 1. Connect & discover classic (V1) tables
Pick a subscription and Log Analytics workspace. The grid below lists every table in the workspace, flags which ones are **Classic** (i.e. still use the legacy HTTP Data Collector API / MMA agent - `schema.tableSubType == 'Classic'`), and shows recent ingestion volume so you can prioritize which tables to migrate first.

| project id, name, subscriptionId, location
| join kind = inner (
    resourcecontainers
    | where type == "microsoft.resources/subscriptions"
    | project subscriptionId, subscription = strcat(name," (",subscriptionId,")")
    )
on subscriptionId
| project value = id, label = name, group = subscription

content.json: **Tip:** This grid only contains **Classic** tables. The ingestion total and sparkline use the selected **Time Range**. Select a row to carry that table into Step 2.
No table is selected yet - select a row in the grid above (**Step 1 result**) to continue.

# 2 | Validate the schema
Selected table: **{SelectedTableName}**. Review the proposed input mapping and any compatibility-mode guidance.

## 2. Inspect the table's current schema
This reads the *live* column list for the selected table and computes:
- **CleanName** - the column name with any legacy type-suffix removed.
- **MappedType** - the KQL/DCR data type for that input column.
- Whether two or more columns collapse to the same `CleanName` (a **collision**).
- **InputName** - the actual DCR input column. If any collision exists, the workbook safely retains all original unique names instead of blocking deployment.

content.query:
let tableDetails = todynamic(base64_decode_tostring("{SelectedTableDetails:base64}"));
let cols = tableDetails.properties.schema.columns;
let reserved = dynamic(["_ResourceId","id","_SubscriptionId","TenantId","Type","UniqueId","Title","RawData","tenant","MG","ManagementGroupName","SourceSystem"]);
let base = print col = cols
    | mv-expand col
    | extend Name = tostring(col.name), Type = tostring(col.type)
    | where Name !in~ (reserved)
    | extend Suffix = extract(@'_(s|d|b|g|t)$', 1, Name)
    | extend Base = extract(@'^(.*)_(?:s|d|b|g|t)$', 1, Name)
    | extend CleanName = iif(isempty(Base), Name, Base)
    | extend MappedType = case(Suffix == "s", "string", Suffix == "d", "real", Suffix == "b", "boolean", Suffix == "g", "string", Suffix == "t", "datetime", Type);
let collisionCount = toscalar(base | summarize Cnt = count() by CleanName | where Cnt > 1 | summarize TotalCollisions = count());
base
| join kind=leftouter (
    base
    | summarize DuplicateCount = count() by CleanName
    ) on CleanName
| extend Collision = DuplicateCount > 1
| extend InputName = iif(collisionCount > 0, Name, CleanName)
| extend Resolution = iif(collisionCount > 0, "Compatibility mode - original names retained", "Clean-name mode")
| project Name, Type, CleanName, InputName, MappedType, Collision, Resolution
| order by Collision desc, CleanName asc
content.title: Current columns -> DCR input-stream mapping

parameters.name: DcrArtifacts

content.json: **Compatibility mode applied:** {CollisionCount} clean column name(s) are ambiguous (for example, `Computer_s` and `Computer_d` both become `Computer`). The source table cannot be changed, so the generated DCR input stream retains the table's original unique column names for every field. No table schema change is required, and deployment can continue. Your Logs Ingestion API payload must use the original suffixed names shown in **InputName**. To use clean names instead, resolve the ambiguity in the sending application before calling the API.

# 3 | Configure the DCR
The input schema is ready. Configure the DCR and choose whether to create or reuse a Data Collection Endpoint.

## 3. Configure the Data Collection Rule
The DCR is created in the **same resource group and region as the workspace** (`{ResourceGroupId}`, `{WorkspaceLocation}`), per Azure Monitor recommended practice. Choose a name, and either create a new Data Collection Endpoint (DCE) or reuse one that already exists in the resource group.

parameters.label: Data Collection Endpoint

paramValidationRules.message: 3-44 letters, numbers or hyphens; cannot start or end with a hyphen

parameters.name: ExistingDce
parameters.label: Existing DCE
parameters.query:
resources
| where type =~ "microsoft.insights/datacollectionendpoints"
| where id startswith "{ResourceGroupId}"
| project value = id, label = name

content.query:
let cols = dynamic({InputColumnsJson});
print col = cols
| mv-expand col
| project ['Input stream column'] = tostring(col.name), ['DCR type'] = tostring(col.type)
content.title: Preview: DCR input stream columns

content.json:
**Transformation KQL** that will run in the DCR. In clean-name mode it restores the table's existing suffixed names; in compatibility mode it remains `source` because input names already match:
```kusto
{TransformKqlText}
```

# 4 | Review and deploy
Open the native ARM deployment to review the hosted template before deploying **{DcrName}**.

## 4. Review & deploy
Use **Review and Deploy Data Collection Rule** to open Azure's native ARM deployment experience. Select **View template** to inspect the hosted template and substituted parameters before deploying the Data Collection Rule and, if selected, a new Data Collection Endpoint.

parameters.name: DeploymentReady

links.linkLabel: Review and Deploy Data Collection Rule

templateRunContext.title: Deploy Data Collection Rule and Endpoint
templateRunContext.description: The template deploys **{DcrName}** and, when requested, **{NewDceName}** into `{ResourceGroupId}`. Use **View template** to inspect the resources and parameter values before deployment. No changes are made to the destination schema for `{SelectedTableName}`.

content.json: **Note:** You need `Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionRules/write` (and, if creating a new DCE, `Microsoft.Insights/dataCollectionEndpoints/write`) permission on the resource group to deploy - for example via the **Monitoring Contributor** built-in role. After deployment, update your ingestion client to call the [Logs ingestion API](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-monitor/logs/logs-ingestion-api-overview) against this DCR instead of the legacy HTTP Data Collector API.
